Location is used in the foreground for timing calculations. No permission is requested on launch, and location is not acquired or stored before an available location flow is completed.

The calculated sunrise-to-sunset interval is divided into 12 equal internal Day Horas. Sunset to the following calculated sunrise is divided independently into 12 equal internal Night Horas. The seven-ruler sequence is Saturn → Jupiter → Mars → Sun → Venus → Mercury → Moon, and the first interval uses the civil weekday ruler.

The approved convention models the apparent upper solar limb at a sea-level, level and unobstructed horizon using a 90.8333° solar-centre zenith distance. It supports civil dates from 1900-01-01 through 2100-12-31 and requires the following day’s sunrise for a complete Hora day. Terrain, mountains, buildings, observer height, weather, horizon obstruction and unusual refraction can make visible events differ. Independent validation uses a 60-second tolerance. These are calculated astronomical times, not observed, exact, certified, or physically millisecond-accurate events.

%1$s is a family-only Android application. Version %2$s, build %3$d. Signing, contact, and update identity remain release-owned and unavailable; credentials are never displayed.

The application presents neutral timing information only. It makes no prediction, advice, auspiciousness, medical, legal, safety, or emergency claim. It has no ads, analytics, account, backend, or required network connection.

Location is intended for foreground timing calculations and approved location data stays on-device. Precise or approximate device use begins only after an explicit action and permission. No location, coordinate, history, account, or analytics data are currently acquired or stored. Settings is the clear-data route; reset remains unavailable until persistence exists. Backup and device transfer must exclude future location data.
The Method screen summarises the approved production and independent validation source roles. Full notices and redistribution obligations remain mandatory before release.

Calculated astronomical sunrise and sunset can differ from visible events because of terrain, buildings, observer height, weather, horizon obstruction, and unusual refraction. Jyotisha is non-authoritative and must not be used for emergencies or safety-critical decisions.
Signing, reproducible build, installation, update, rollback, contact, and release validation remain mandatory release obligations. No signing credentials or private release material are displayed.
